findings.problem: TokenWorkflow.status is a public String field, allowing any string value including illegal lifecycle states like "bogus", "", or conflicting values alongside is_validated/is_sent flags.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct a TokenWorkflow with an invalid or contradictory status string, breaking all workflow invariants at the type level with no compiler enforcement.
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with a sealed enum TokenStatus { Created, Validated, Sent } and remove the redundant is_validated/is_sent booleans. Remove or hide the TokenWorkflow constructor so status can only be set through typed transitions.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are public booleans encoding lifecycle state. Booleans cannot express ordering or mutual exclusion (e.g., is_validated=true and is_sent=false with status="sent" is contradictory).
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set is_validated=true while leaving status as "created", creating an inconsistent workflow state that runtime checks would need to guard against but the type system cannot.
findings.fix: Replace both bools with a single TokenStatus enum that encodes the full lifecycle state. Use typestates (e.g., TokenCreated, TokenValidated, TokenSent) to make the lifecycle order enforceable at compile time.

findings.problem: TokenWorkflow.id is a public String with no domain newtype. Any caller can pass empty, malformed, or otherwise invalid IDs directly into the workflow without boundary validation.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream consumers of TokenWorkflow cannot assume id is a valid identifier. Validation must be repeated at every use site instead of being guaranteed by construction.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype TokenId(String) with a fallible constructor that validates the id at the boundary, then use TokenId inside TokenWorkflow.

findings.problem: All fields of TokenWorkflow are pub, meaning any code can mutate fields directly without going through workflow transition logic. The struct has no constructor and no encapsulation.
findings.failure_mode: Direct field mutation bypasses any transition guards, allowing illegal state transitions (e.g., setting is_sent=true without calling mark_sent, or changing status after mark_sent).
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a fallible constructor and transition methods that enforce the state machine. Mark fields as `#[allow(dead_code)]` only if needed for serialization boundaries.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes an owned TokenWorkflow and blindly overwrites status and is_sent regardless of the current state. It does not check whether the token is already sent, validated, or in any other state.
findings.failure_mode: A token already in Sent state can be marked_sent again (idempotency violation), or a token that has never been validated can be marked sent (state machine violation).
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept the source typestate (e.g., TokenValidated) and return the destination typestate (e.g., TokenSent). This makes the transition the only way to produce a sent token.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses `.to_string()` to allocate a new String for status. In a pure core this is acceptable but the allocation is unbounded and there is no try_reserve or checked capacity pattern.
findings.failure_mode: Under memory pressure, the to_string allocation could fail silently via OOM rather than returning a typed allocation error that callers can handle.
findings.fix: If the set of status values is finite and known, use an enum (see BLOCKER fixes) to eliminate the allocation entirely. If a String is unavoidable, use a fallible constructor or try_reserve pattern.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for the TokenWorkflow workflow. No allocation profiling or second-ring latency evidence is present.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics of the workflow (allocation pressure from String status, cache behavior of the struct) are unmeasured and unbounded.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark crate or #[bench] test measuring mark_sent throughput and allocation count under criterion.

findings.problem: No evidence of cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test execution.
findings.failure_mode: Code style, clippy warnings, and behavioral correctness are unverified.
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, and cargo test; report results.

residual_risk: The TokenWorkflow struct allows any illegal state by construction. All fields are public primitives with no typestate enforcement, no constructor, and mark_sent performs no state checks. This is the highest-severity class of defect in Holzman Rust — the type system provides zero protection against workflow invariants. Without enum-based typestates and private fields, every caller is a potential violation source. Static review only; no commands run.
